_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Eswatini covering Nguni migration, Dlamini dynasty, Mswati II expansion, British protectorate (Swaziland), independence 1968, Mswati III absolute monarchy (last absolute monarch in Africa), Reed Dance ceremony, and pro-democracy protests.

ethnic_groups.name: Swazi (Ngwane/Dlamini)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bantu Nguni-speaking; organized into clans under Dlamini royal house; siSwati language; include core clans: Dlamini, Nkambule, Hlophe, Matsebula

ethnic_groups.name: Zulu
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern border; related Nguni people; some pre-date Swazi state formation; isiZulu mutually intelligible with siSwati

ethnic_groups.name: Tsonga/Shangaan
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern lowveld; originally from Mozambique/southern coastal region; distinct language and customs

ethnic_groups.name: Sotho
ethnic_groups.notes: Small presence; cross-border with South Africa and Lesotho

ethnic_groups.name: White/European
ethnic_groups.notes: Predominantly South African and British descent; significant landholding

ethnic_groups.name: Asian/Indian
ethnic_groups.notes: Small commercial community; mostly Indian origin

ethnic_groups.name: Mixed/Other
ethnic_groups.notes: Includes Coloured community and other minorities

natural_resources.notes: Small economy; sugar dominant agricultural export; Coca-Cola concentrate plant (largest private employer); soft drink concentrate one of top exports; forestry (pine/eucalyptus plantations); Havelock asbestos mine closed (health hazard); diamond mine at Dvokolwako

military.notes: Last absolute monarchy in Africa; security forces deployed against pro-democracy protests 2021; Umbutfo Eswatini Defence Force small but equipped; no external threats; internal security primary focus; regiment system (age-set) traditional

infrastructure.notes: Landlocked; dependent on Mozambique/South Africa for trade routes.

debt_aid.notes: South African Customs Union (SACU) revenues critical (~50% government revenue); heavily dependent on South Africa economically; HIV/AIDS spending significant (highest HIV prevalence globally ~27%); monarchy's spending vs public services tension

education.notes: Free primary education since 2010; high literacy; English-language instruction; student protests often lead to broader pro-democracy movement; many study in South Africa; Waterford Kamhlaba United World College produces Pan-African leaders

diaspora_migration.notes: Mainly South Africa migration (economic, HIV treatment access); porous border with Mozambique; small but growing exile community (pro-democracy activists); seasonal laborers in South African mines

digital_economy.notes: Small but growing tech sector; Royal Science & Technology Park government initiative; MTN Eswatini dominant; internet costs declining; government digitization lagging; proximity to South Africa brings tech spillover

country_profile.notes_unique: Africa's last absolute monarchy; renamed from Swaziland to Eswatini in 2018; the annual Umhlanga (Reed Dance) ceremony involves tens of thousands of young women.
country_profile.national_anthem: Nkulunkulu Mnikati wetibusiso temaSwati (O God, Bestower of the Blessings of the Swazi)

geography.terrain: Mountainous in west (Highveld); hilly in center (Middleveld); plains in east (Lowveld and Lubombo Plateau)
geography.notes: One of smallest countries in Africa; last absolute monarchy; dual capital (Mbabane administrative, Lobamba legislative/royal).

economy_extended.notes: SACU revenue (~50% government income); sugar, soft drink concentrate (Coca-Cola), and textile exports; lilangeni pegged to South African rand.

health.notes: World's highest HIV prevalence (26% adults); significant progress with ART coverage (>90%); TB-HIV co-infection major challenge.

food_agriculture.notes: Sugar dominant cash crop (4th largest in Africa); Swazi Nation Land (SNL) communal farming; commercial estates for sugar.

energy.notes: Imports ~80% electricity from South Africa and Mozambique; bagasse (sugarcane waste) significant; solar expansion planned.

transport.notes: Landlocked; rail link to Mozambique (Maputo port) for exports; new international airport opened 2014.

tourism.notes: Cultural tourism (Swazi ceremonies); game reserves; often combined with South Africa/Mozambique trips.

human_rights_gender.lgbtq_legal_status: Illegal (common law; not enforced for women)
human_rights_gender.notes: Last absolute monarchy in Africa; 2021 pro-democracy protests violently suppressed; political parties banned in national elections; king controls all three branches.

security_stability.notes: 2021 pro-democracy uprising; internet shutdowns during protests; SADC mediation attempted.

cultural_heritage.media_landscape: State-dominated; Times of Eswatini; Swazi TV; some private media but restricted
cultural_heritage.notes: Last absolute monarchy in Africa; Swazi cultural ceremonies are major national identity markers; polygamy practiced by royals.

legal_system.legal_tradition: Mixed: Roman-Dutch common law and Swazi customary law
legal_system.customary_law_role: Central to governance (Tinkhundla system); Swazi National Courts
legal_system.notes: Dual legal system; Tinkhundla governance system (constituencies); king appoints PM and much of parliament; Swazi National Courts (customary).

comparative_rankings._note: Country position relative to continent and global.

current_leader.name: King Mswati III
current_leader.title: King (Ingwenyama)
current_leader.notes: Africa's last absolute monarch; crowned at age 18; son of Sobhuza II; 15+ wives; pro-democracy protests 2021 violently suppressed

queen_mother.name: Ntfombi Tfwala
queen_mother.title: Indlovukazi (Queen Mother/She-Elephant)
queen_mother.notes: Serves as co-head of state and regent; dual monarchy tradition

former_monarchs.name: Ngwane III
former_monarchs.notes: Led Ngwane people southward from Mozambique; eponymous founder of the Swazi nation

former_monarchs.name: Sobhuza I (Somhlolo)
former_monarchs.notes: Led nation during Mfecane; moved Swazi heartland to Ezulwini Valley; prophesied arrival of white people

former_monarchs.name: Mswati II
former_monarchs.notes: Greatest military king; expanded Swazi territory to its widest extent; nation named after him

former_monarchs.name: Sobhuza II
former_monarchs.notes: World's longest-reigning monarch (82 years including regency); abolished Westminster constitution 1973; died with 70+ wives and 210 children

910.name: Early Inhabitants and Stone Age Settlements
910.description: Early Stone Age occupation evidenced by tools at sites across Eswatini; San hunter-gatherers leave rock art; Ngwenya Mine is one of the world's oldest known mines.

sub_clusters.name: Ngwenya Iron Ore Mine (Ancient)
sub_clusters.description: One of the world's oldest mines; San peoples mined haematite (red ochre) for cosmetic and ritual use around 43,000 years ago.

920.name: Nguni Migration and Dlamini Dynasty Origins
920.description: Nguni-speaking Bantu peoples migrate into the region; the Dlamini clan emerges as the ruling dynasty, establishing one of Africa's oldest continuous monarchies.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu Migration and Settlement
sub_clusters.description: Nguni-speaking Bantu peoples arrive from East Africa via Mozambique; introduce iron-working, cattle herding, and agriculture; displace or absorb San populations.

930.name: Formation of the Swazi Kingdom
930.description: The Swazi kingdom crystallises under Ngwane III and expands dramatically under Sobhuza I and Mswati II, navigating the turbulent Mfecane era.

sub_clusters.description: Ngwane III (considered the first king of Swaziland) leads the Dlamini across the Lubombo Mountains into present-day Eswatini; establishes the kingdom's territorial core.
